items.q: Well-defined salmon-pink plaques with silvery scale on elbows and knees that bleed on grattage indicate?
items.exp: Plaque psoriasis favours extensors with micaceous scale, Auspitz bleeding and Koebner spread.
r: Incorrect. That is orange-red with islands of sparing.
Incorrect. That is photosensitive annular with scale.
Correct. Extensor silvery plaques with Auspitz.
Incorrect. That has violaceous papules with striae.

items.q: A teenager erupts in small drop-like scaly papules on the trunk two weeks after streptococcal sore throat. This is?
items.exp: Guttate psoriasis follows streptococcal pharyngitis with abrupt raindrop papules that may resolve or evolve to plaque disease.
r: Incorrect. That gives tiny shiny papules.
Correct. Post-streptococcal drop lesions.
Incorrect. That starts with a herald patch.
Incorrect. Exanthems lack silvery scale.
items.kp: Raindrop rash after sore throat is guttate psoriasis.

items.q: Nail pits, oil-drop discolouration and onycholysis in a patient with scaly elbow plaques suggest?
o: Psoriatic nail disease with arthritis risk
items.exp: Psoriatic nails show pitting, salmon patches and onycholysis, marking higher risk of psoriatic arthritis.
r: Correct. Pits plus oil drops flag psoriasis.
Incorrect. That gives subungual debris without pits.
Incorrect. That thins nails with pterygium.
Incorrect. That gives fine regular pits only.
items.kp: Pitted oily nails with plaques mean psoriasis.

items.q: Generalised sterile lakes of pus on red skin with fever after steroid withdrawal fits?
items.exp: Von Zumbusch pustular psoriasis is a febrile emergency with lakes of sterile pus, often triggered by withdrawal or hypocalcaemia.
r: Incorrect. AGEP is drug-triggered and shorter.
Incorrect. That is staphylococcal in children.
Incorrect. That gives annular half-pustules chronically.
Correct. Febrile lakes of pus on erythema.
items.kp: Febrile pus lakes mean pustular psoriasis.

items.q: Whole-body redness with scaling, shivering and ankle swelling in a known psoriatic suggests?
items.exp: Erythroderma covers over 90 percent of skin with thermoregulatory, protein and fluid loss needing inpatient care.
r: Incorrect. That evolves slowly with atypical cells.
Incorrect. That adds eosinophilia and organ injury.
Correct. Universal red scaling in a psoriatic.
Incorrect. Eczema erythroderma lacks psoriatic history.

items.q: A psoriatic has sausage digits, distal interphalangeal arthritis and a pencil-in-cup radiograph. The pattern is?
items.exp: Psoriatic arthritis attacks DIPs with dactylitis, enthesitis and pencil-in-cup deformity, typically rheumatoid-factor negative.
r: Incorrect. That gives Heberden nodes without sausage digits.
Correct. DIP disease with dactylitis.
Incorrect. That spares DIPs with positive factor.
Incorrect. That gives tophi with punched-out erosions.
items.kp: Sausage digits with DIP disease mean psoriatic arthritis.

items.q: Biopsy of a plaque shows regular acanthosis with parakeratosis and Munro microabscesses. This histology is?
items.exp: Psoriasis histology combines regular rete elongation, absent granular layer, parakeratosis and neutrophil collections.
r: Correct. Regular acanthosis with Munro abscesses.
Incorrect. That shows saw-tooth rete with Civatte bodies.
Incorrect. That shows focal parakeratosis with extravasated red cells.
Incorrect. That shows spongiosis with vesicles.

items.q: First-line topical care for limited plaque psoriasis uses which pairing?
o: Vitamin D analogue with a topical corticosteroid
items.exp: Vitamin D analogues plus topical steroids are the standard first-line topical combination for limited plaques.
r: Incorrect. Infection is not the driver.
Incorrect. Sunscreen alone does not clear plaques.
Incorrect. Systemic steroids flare psoriasis on withdrawal.
Correct. Standard topical pairing.
items.kp: Limited plaques need vitamin D plus steroid.

items.q: Widespread psoriasis unresponsive to topicals and phototherapy steps up to which systemic class group?
o: Methotrexate, ciclosporin or acitretin classes with monitoring
items.exp: Conventional systemics with organ monitoring control extensive disease; steroids alone rebound and antibiotics do not treat psoriasis.
r: Incorrect. Antifungals have no role.
Incorrect. Steroid monotherapy flares on taper.
Correct. Monitored conventional systemics.
Incorrect. Antibiotics treat infection, not psoriasis.

items.q: A psoriatic with metabolic syndrome needs counselling that psoriasis associates with?
o: Cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidity needing screening
items.exp: Psoriasis is a systemic inflammatory state linked with metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular events, arthritis and mood disorders.
r: Incorrect. Anaemia alone misses the syndrome.
Correct. Screen beyond the skin.
Incorrect. Associations are well established.
Incorrect. Joints are only one comorbidity.
